questions: When sorting alphabetically for tie-breaking, is the sorting case-sensitive (i.e., 'apple' before 'Banana' based on ASCII/Unicode code points) or case-insensitive?
For tie-breaking, does alphabetical sorting apply to all data types (e.g., numbers, booleans) or only to strings? If non-strings, what ordering is used?
When a column contains only empty strings, is the most common value considered to be the empty string (since empty strings are distinct values)?
If a column has all values missing (e.g., NaN or None due to type inference), how should that be handled? Are missing values considered distinct from empty strings?
For tie-breaking, if multiple values have the same frequency, does alphabetical sorting consider the raw value (e.g., integer 10 vs string '10') or a string representation?
Is the CSV file guaranteed to have a header row? If not, how should column names be determined?
Should the function handle CSV files with varying numbers of columns per row (ragged rows)? If so, how are missing values treated?
What delimiter should be assumed for the CSV file? Is it always a comma, or could it vary (e.g., tabs, semicolons)?
